rationale: Both miss the ground-truth reviewer's actual asks (explicit comment/check on parent-first ordering, running the specific benchmark test, fixing precommit), so recall is low and roughly tied. X piles on speculative/alarmist findings (treating red buildkite npu/amd CI as a 'major' merge-blocker, hypothetical pipeline.py:555 dict/list mismatch, silent-truncation footgun) that aren't corroborated by the diff or the actual outcome (the PR was approved and merged with only a precommit nit), hurting precision despite being very actionable with concrete pytest commands. Y reaches the same verified conclusions (parent-first ordering confirmed via orchestrator, dict|None contract compatible with all consumers) but calibrates its verdict to APPROVE with balanced non-blocking notes, which better matches the ground-truth reviewers' actual LGTM outcome, giving it higher precision at a small actionability cost.
